title: Ranking with Slot Constraints

problem.claim: The paper studies ranking for human decision-making processes with slot constraints, where candidates are evaluated for slot eligibility in ranking order and the objective is to maximize the number of filled slots.

gap.claim: Naive adaptations of the Probability Ranking Principle can be highly sub-optimal for slot-constrained ranking problems.

contributions.claim: The paper formalizes the slot-constrained ranking problem.
The paper introduces MatchRank, a ranking algorithm that generalizes the Probability Ranking Principle and subsumes it when there are no slot constraints.
The paper provides a strong approximation guarantee for MatchRank without independence assumptions between slots or candidates.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MatchRank can be implemented efficiently.
The authors report substantial improvements over a range of synthetic and real-world tasks in empirical evaluations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Rankings are used to allocate reviewing resources in human decision-making processes.
Many such processes involve complex constraints, including limited slots for majors or stratified medical-trial cohorts.
The slot-constrained ranking problem is defined as maximizing filled slots when eligibility is evaluated in ranking order.
The paper identifies limitations of naive PRP adaptations and introduces MatchRank, which generalizes PRP.
The authors report theoretical guarantees, efficient implementation, and empirical improvements on synthetic and real-world tasks.

source_observation.claim: Naive adaptations of PRP can be highly sub-optimal under slot constraints.

interpretation.claim: Introducing explicit constraints can require ranking objectives and algorithms that differ from unconstrained relevance-based ranking.

application.claim: When ranking candidates for constrained allocation, evaluate whether the ranking method accounts for slot interactions rather than applying an unconstrained ranking principle directly.

exception.claim: MatchRank subsumes PRP when there are no slot constraints, so a specialized constrained method may not be necessary in the unconstrained case.
